extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and publication criteria for authors preparing and submitting original research manuscripts to the PLOS ONE journal, including acceptable article types, ethical and reporting requirements, and standards for methods, results, and language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of original research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate original research across natural sciences, medical research, engineering, and related social sciences and humanities. PLOS ONE will not consider reviews, case reports, study protocols, hypothesis/proposal papers, letters/commentaries/essays, opinion pieces, policy papers, clinical practice guidelines, other secondary literature, monographs, or unsolicited collection reviews/overviews. Acceptable submissions include systematic reviews (only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling), descriptions of methods/software/databases/tools (if following appropriate reporting guidelines), qualitative research (if adhering to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines), and studies reporting negative results. Submissions describing these acceptable types must follow submission-specific requirements as noted in the submission guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not accept studies already published, in whole or in part, in the peer-reviewed literature. All manuscript figures should be original and not previously published. Submissions currently under consideration elsewhere will not be accepted. Manuscripts deposited in preprint servers (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv), published as a thesis, or presented at conferences are acceptable and do not affect consideration. If a study replicates or is very similar to previous work, authors must provide a sound scientific rationale, clearly reference and discuss prior literature, and justify the contribution; otherwise such submissions will likely be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical rigor and methods detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must be conducted rigorously with appropriate controls and replication. Sample sizes should be large enough to produce robust results where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described sufficiently for another researcher to reproduce the experiments. Statistical analyses should meet high technical standards and be reported with enough detail for evaluation and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript's data must support the conclusions drawn. Submissions will be rejected if interpretation is unjustified or inappropriate; authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Authors may discuss possible implications but must clearly identify these as hypotheses rather than definitive conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts, so submitted language must be clear, correct, and unambiguous. Papers with difficult-to-understand language or many errors may be rejected or authors may be advised to seek independent editorial/manuscript editing services prior to revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics of experimentation and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research must be conducted to the highest ethical standards; PLOS ONE may apply standards more stringent than local ones. Approval from relevant bodies is required for studies involving humans (including observational/survey/personal data), animals (including observational studies), non-commercial cell lines, field sampling, and studies with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. PLOS ONE follows COPE Code of Conduct and Best Practice Guidelines; authors must comply with publication ethics best practices regarding authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. Concerns should be addressed to the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines and data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results must be reported rigorously and in accordance with discipline-specific reporting guidelines (see submission guidelines for details). Authors must follow community standards for data deposition in publicly available resources (e.g., gene sequences, microarray expression, structural studies). Failure to comply with data-sharing/community deposition standards may result in rejection. See PLOS ONE's data availability policy for detailed requirements.
